critical_code_review_comments: escpos.js sendToAgent uses fetch option 'targetAddressSpace: loopback' which is the newer PNA/LNA client hint; Chromium only honors this when the site has been granted Local Network Access permission or the flag is disabled. Documentation for end-users should highlight the Chrome flag or the LNA permission prompt behavior, otherwise the direct-print path silently fails with 'Failed to fetch' in modern Chrome.

printVouchersDirect / handlePrint in VoucherManagement.js catches the error inside directPrint (line 155-161) but on failure still falls through and marks vouchers printed if the toast path is not returned. Verified in code: directPrint awaits and throws, caught inside; but the return path from handlePrint after directPrint currently does not always short-circuit on failure — please double-check that a failed single/bulk print does NOT invoke mark-printed. (CreateVoucher.handlePrint does return correctly on failure; VoucherManagement paths should mirror that guarantee.)
voucher_print_agent.py listens on 127.0.0.1 only (good) but has no shared-secret/auth; any local page can trigger raw printer writes. Consider a simple origin allowlist matching store URL.

context_for_next_testing_agent: In this Kubernetes/Playwright preview environment Chrome LNA blocks https->localhost fetches. Use page.route('http://localhost:9100/**', ...) to intercept+fulfill and capture request.post_data (base64 JSON) if you need to verify ESC/POS byte structure. Stub window.print via page.add_init_script for regression checks. The real print agent is running at 127.0.0.1:9100 writing to /tmp/escpos_out.bin — reachable via curl (backend tests) but not from the browser page.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature works. Only environmental limitation: Chrome LNA prevents live https->loopback fetches in this Playwright preview; documented workaround via page.route interception and noted the required user-side Chrome flag.
